findings.problem: With exactly one installed `ask-ollama` bridge family and one valid endpoint record that has no `default_model`, the installer creates no `local` profile but still writes the single-profile Ollama ladder. That ladder names a missing profile, making the generated file invalid and every review refuse.
findings.suggestion: Only emit the Ollama ladder when its `local` profile was created; otherwise omit the ladder and report that the owner must select a configured chat model.

findings.problem: Profiles may pass every option that a bridge declares as review-usable, but the decision does not reserve the engine-owned `timeout` and `schema` options. A bridge declaration could therefore permit a profile to supply `--timeout`, defeating item 11's stated 20-second action-review bridge limit (and potentially collide with schema handling).
findings.suggestion: Explicitly reserve `timeout` and `schema` (and any other engine-owned options) from profile options, and require the module declaration to reject those names.

findings.problem: A multi-rung `default` ladder can apply to `action-review` when that kind has no explicit ladder, despite the decision requiring an action-review ladder to contain exactly one rung. The document does not say whether such a configuration is rejected or which constraint wins.
findings.suggestion: Specify that an action-review ladder resolved through `default` must have exactly one rung, or require an explicit one-rung `action-review` ladder whenever `default` has more than one rung.

summary: The proposed profile format has three unresolved cases that can produce an invalid generated configuration or violate its action-review time-bound and ladder rules.
